chunks: Jurara narrated from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Regarding one who resides in Mecca for two years, he is considered from the people of Mecca and has no right to al-Mat'ah (shortening of prayer). I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'What if he has family in Iraq and family in Mecca?' He said, 'Let him see which group is dominant over him; he is from their people.'

key_terms.الْمُتْعَةَ: Al-Mat'ah (provision/right to shorten prayer for travelers)

ai.seo_question: How does a Muslim determine if they are considered a resident or a traveler for prayer purposes when they have family in multiple cities?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Baqir (AS) to define the threshold of 'residency' (Iqamah) for shortening prayers, establishing a two-year period as the standard for losing traveler status. The narration further refines this by introducing the concept of 'dominant attachment' (Ghalib), where familial ties serve as the decisive factor in determining one's primary residence when multiple homes exist, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the early Shia community.
